intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Monty pulls a crumpled watering list out of a cardigan pocket. It has soil on it.

teach0.speaker: python
teach0.text: Can I show you my favorite thing in all of programming? It's not even code. It's comments.

teach1.speaker: python
teach1.text: A comment is a note for people. In Python, anything after a # is skipped. The computer never reads it, but the next person always does.

teach2.speaker: python
teach2.text: You can also put a # in front of a line of code to switch it off without deleting it. Readability counts. So does not losing things.

passed.speaker: python
passed.text: See? Python reads the code, people read the notes, and everyone gets along. And the cactus is remembered. Thank you, {player}.

failed.speaker: python
failed.text: Hm. Python's still tripping over something. It's okay! Want to look at it again?

bye.speaker: python
bye.text: No rush. The list isn't going anywhere. Neither am I.
